skill.name: nansen-wallet-profiler
skill.description: Profile blockchain wallets with Nansen CLI commands for balances, labels, PnL, transactions, counterparties, related wallets, traces, batches, and comparisons.
skill.summary: Profile crypto wallets with Nansen CLI commands for balances, labels, PnL, transactions, relationships, traces, and comparisons.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. The external command hits are Markdown code spans or fences documenting Nansen CLI usage, and the env hits only declare NANSEN_API_KEY as required configuration. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden override instructions were found.

remediation.issue: API key handling is documented only as required metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add setup guidance that tells users to keep NANSEN_API_KEY in environment variables and never paste it into prompts.

remediation.issue: Trace and batch commands can consume many Nansen API calls.
remediation.suggestion: Keep conservative defaults visible and ask users to confirm large depth, width, or batch runs.

remediation.issue: Batch mode can read wallet addresses from a local file path.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to confirm the intended file path before using the documented --file option.

static_findings.snippet: | `--chain` | Required except for perps and search |
| `--width` | Trace width — keep low to save credits |
- `pnl-summary` has no pagination support (returns aggregate stats, not a list).
- `labels` has no pagination support — the API ignores `per_page` and always returns all labels for
- `trace` makes many API calls — use `--width` conservatively.
- `batch` accepts `--file <path>` with one address per line as alternative to `--addresses`.

content.value_statement: Wallet investigations require many repeated Nansen CLI calls across balances, labels, PnL, and relationships. This skill organizes those workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.
actual_capabilities: Profile wallet balances, labels, PnL, transactions, and historical balances through Nansen CLI commands.
Search identity labels and compare two wallets for shared counterparties and tokens.
Run batch profiles from comma-separated addresses or an address file.
Trace related wallets and counterparties with configurable depth and width.
Export or format results with table, field, and CSV options.
limitations: Requires an installed nansen CLI and a valid NANSEN_API_KEY.
Results depend on Nansen API coverage, rate limits, and plan permissions.
Trace and batch workflows can consume many API credits.
It does not validate blockchain addresses beyond the CLI behavior.

use_cases.title: Portfolio Investigation
use_cases.description: Review one wallet balance, labels, transactions, and PnL before deeper research.

use_cases.title: Counterparty Mapping
use_cases.description: Find related wallets and counterparties for a focused address review.

use_cases.title: Batch Wallet Review
use_cases.description: Run repeatable profiles across a list of addresses and compare shared signals.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Wallet Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nansen-wallet-profiler to get labels, balance, and 30-day PnL for this Ethereum address: <address>.

prompt_templates.title: Transaction Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review recent activity on another chain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile <address> on Solana. Show recent transactions, historical balances for 30 days, and any notable labels.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Wallets
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these Ethereum wallets for shared counterparties and tokens: <address one>, <address two>. Summarize overlaps and differences.

prompt_templates.title: Constrained Trace Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a bounded multi-hop relationship review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace counterparties for <address> on Ethereum with depth 2 and width 5. Include labels, balance, and PnL only when available.

output_examples.input: Profile an Ethereum wallet for labels, balances, and 30-day PnL.
output_examples.output: A concise wallet summary with known labels, current balances, token exposure, PnL, and caveats about missing data.

output_examples.input: Compare two wallets for shared counterparties.
output_examples.output: A comparison brief listing overlapping counterparties, common tokens, and differences that may need follow-up.

output_examples.input: Trace related wallets with low width.
output_examples.output: A scoped relationship map with one or two hops, ranked counterparties, and notes on API credit use.

best_practices: Confirm chain and address format before running high-volume commands.
Start trace workflows with low depth and width to control API credits.
Keep NANSEN_API_KEY in environment variables, not in prompts or chat history.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, seed phrases, or private wallet material into prompts.
Do not run broad traces before defining a research question and budget.
Do not treat labels or PnL estimates as final compliance conclusions.

faq.question: What data source does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the installed Nansen CLI and the user Nansen API access.

faq.question: Does it need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares NANSEN_API_KEY as required environment configuration.

faq.question: Can it compare wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents compare, counterparty, related wallet, and batch workflows.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: The documented flags include table, field selection, and CSV format options.

faq.question: Does it work for every chain?
faq.answer: No. Most commands require a supported chain, and perps and search have different requirements.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize wallet analytics and should be reviewed by qualified users.
